A.scene: A wide scene of Jesus giving a child a place in the midst of the disciples, seen from a gently elevated diagonal viewpoint. Arrange a broken oval of three adult presences around a small standing child, with Jesus seated near the upper left so his attentive gaze approaches the child rather than towering above. The child is slightly right of center, in a simple pale garment, feet naturally grounded, hands relaxed at the sides. A large quiet ivory shape enters from the lower left and changes direction near the child's feet, meeting deep aubergine and warm stone shapes that leave the actual room undefined. Several peripheral adult shoulders and hems dissolve into these shapes, while each visible face and hand remains legible. Use a daring asymmetrical arrangement with diagonal intervals, never a row of standing adults or a frontal child-and-Jesus group copied from the references. No hugging, head patting, decorative angels or house doorway.
A.scripture_relation: Matthew 18:2 and 10: the child is placed in the midst and must not be treated as unimportant. A formerly peripheral small person becomes the hinge of the whole composition, while the larger adults turn and make space. The elevated diagonal viewpoint and seated listening posture are artistic interpretation.

B.scene: An intimate horizontal exchange within a vertical painting. Show the child's painted three-quarter face near the right third, turned left toward the softly cropped profile of Jesus at the left edge. Both are at nearly the same eye height. A narrow irregular ivory interval separates their profiles; below it the child's small open hand rests on their own lap, not holding an adult sleeve. Jesus has a softened brow and patient, slightly parted lips as he listens; the child is alert and unafraid, not smiling for a portrait. Let a broad charcoal-aubergine shape absorb the lower garments, with one restrained dusty-rose passage joining shoulder to space. Faces have clearly visible curved brush drawing and soft mixed-pigment edges while eyes and mouths remain complete. Do not use the previous diagonal adult-over-child composition, sleeve grip, glossy skin or monumental adult portrait.
B.scripture_relation: Do not despise one of these little ones is conveyed by taking the child seriously: equal eye level, an unhurried listening expression, and an open unforced posture. This eye-level encounter is a pictorial interpretation, not an extra event quoted as Gospel.

C.scene: A subjective viewpoint from the small child's place among the disciples. Jesus is seated several steps away near the right half of the painting, visible from head to below the knees, leaning only slightly toward the viewer and meeting the viewer's eyes. His hands rest naturally and openly on his own knees; no hand reaches at the lens. A large cropped adult garment is a narrow peripheral shape along the far left edge only. Another disciple is indicated in the middle distance by a modest head-and-shoulder shape turned toward Jesus. Let an irregular near-white interval cross the middle of the picture like space opening for the child, framed by restrained rose-gray and deep charcoal-aubergine masses that never resolve into a literal hallway. Keep the near foreground almost entirely a quiet painted plane, with no giant body parts or another child seen from behind. The face is small but its attention is unmistakable, completely painted rather than photographic. Compose a spacious psychological encounter, not a close-up face looking at a camera.
C.scripture_relation: The reader occupies the position of a little one who has been brought into the gathering and is now regarded attentively. The opening interval and the seated adult gaze make room for the viewer rather than making the adult visually overpower them. Viewpoint and pose are artistic interpretations of Matthew 18:2 and 10.
